Chapter 6: The Shape of Stories—Understanding Narrative Structure.
Now that we've explored the building blocks of writing, let’s zoom out and look at the bigger picture—the patterns and shapes that hold stories together. Think of narrative structure as the hidden framework, quietly supporting everything that happens, whether a story plays out in a single afternoon or stretches across generations.
If you’re hoping to write your own stories, learning to spot these patterns is a real game-changer.
At its heart, narrative structure is all about how events are arranged, and how each new revelation unfolds at just the right moment. It’s what separates a story that wanders aimlessly from one that pulls you forward, making you want to know what happens next.
If you pay close attention as you read, you’ll start to notice this invisible framework—the way a story’s beginning sets up the world, the middle ramps up tension, and the ending delivers a sense of resolution or transformation.
Here’s a simple way to picture it: imagine a story as a winding journey. The opening pages are like the trailhead, where you meet the landscape and the travelers. As you move into the middle, the path gets tougher—obstacles pop up, choices need to be made, and things get interesting. Then, at the end, you finally arrive and everything falls into place—the meaning of the journey becomes clear.
If you want some practical ways to spot and work with narrative structure, try these:
First, look for the inciting incident—that moment that shakes things up and sets the story in motion.
Next, track the rising and falling action. Watch how the tension builds, then lets up, creating that feeling of momentum.
Pay attention to the turning points—those big decisions or surprises that send the story in a new direction.
And finally, reflect on the resolution. Ask yourself how the ending ties together the themes, character journeys, and any lingering questions.
Of course, writers love to play with structure, too. Some stories move in a straight line, while others jump back in time or switch between different points of view. If you start reading with an eye for structure, you’ll see so many possibilities—and you’ll get to choose the shape that best fits your own story.
But here’s something to remember: understanding narrative structure isn’t about following a strict set of rules. It’s about seeing the patterns that give stories their power and emotional punch. When you read closely and thoughtfully, you’ll start to notice how master storytellers shape their tales—and you’ll learn to do the same with your own, bringing intention and artistry to every page.
